slang.note: Warm Gulf/Saudi greeting for someone you are glad to see; fine for a friendly stranger.

how_are_you.note: Shown for a man; to a woman say kayf haaluki (كيف حالكِ).

slang.note: Everyday Gulf/Saudi casual greeting; to a woman say shlonich (شلونچ). Fine with acquaintances and friendly strangers.

please.note: Shown for a man; to a woman say min fadliki (من فضلِك).

excuse_me.note: The more formal MSA choice for getting attention or passing by; afwan (عفواً) is the more casual everyday alternative and is also used as a reply to thanks.

sorry.note: Shown for a man; a woman says aasifa (آسفة).

slang.note: Warm exclamation of delight or admiration; safe and common with anyone.

delicious.note: MSA dh (ذ) as in "this"; Gulf/Saudi colloquial speech often shifts this to z, heard as la-ZEEZ.

cheers.note: Said after a meal or drink (health, not alcohol); Saudi social norms are dry.
